annotations.title: The foundation of penance.
annotations.text: ◦ Vve ſee hereby, vvhat the firſt groundes of Chriſtian inſtitution or Catechiſme were in the primitiue Church, and that there vvas euer a neceſſarie inſtruction and beleefe of certaine points had by word of mouth and tradition, before men came to the Scriptures: which could not treate of things ſo particularly, as vvas requiſite for the teaching of al neceſſarie groundes. Among theſe points were the 12 Articles conteined in the Apoſtles Creede: the doctrine of penance before Baptiſme: the maner and neceſsitie of Baptiſme: the Sacrament of Impoſition of hands after Baptiſme, called Confirmation: the articles of the Reſurrection, Iudgement, and ſuch like. Vvithout which things firſt laid, if one ſhould be ſent to picke his faith out of the Scripture, there would be madde rule quickly. See S. Auguſtine in expoſt. inchoat. ep. ad Ro. verſus finem.

notes.text: The Apostles forme of Catechisme, and the points therof.

annotations.title: Impoſſible.
annotations.text: [1] How hard the holy Scriptures be, and how dangerouſly they be read of the vnlearned, or of the proud be they neuer ſo wel learned, this one place might teach vs. [2] Wherat the Nouatians of old did ſo ſtumble, that they thought, and heretically taught, that none falling into any mortal ſinne after Baptiſme, could be receiued to mercie or penance in the Church: and ſo to a contentious man, that would folow his owne ſenſe, or the bare wordes, vvithout regard of the Churches ſenſe and rule of faith (after which euery Scripture muſt be expounded) the Apoſtles ſpeach doth here ſound. [3] Euen as to the ſimple, and to the Heretike that ſubmitteth not his ſenſe to the Churches iudgement, certaine places of this ſame Epiſtle, ſeeme at the firſt ſight, to ſtand againſt the daily oblation or ſacrifice of the Maſſe: which yet in truth make no more for that purpoſe, then this text we now ſtand on, ſerueth the Nouatians: as when we come to the places, it ſhal be declared. And let the good Readers beware here alſo of the Proteſtants expoſition, for they are herein worſe then Nouatians, ſpecially ſuch as preciſely folow Caluin: [4] holding impiouſly, that it is impoſſible for one that forſaketh entirely his faith, that is, becommeth an Apoſtata or an Heretike, to be receiued to penance or to Gods mercie. To eſtabliſh vvhich falſe and damnable ſenſe, theſe fellowes make nothing of S. Ambroſes, S. Chryſoſtoms, and the other fathers expoſition, [5]which is the holy Churches ſenſe, [6] That the Apoſtle meaneth of that penance which is done before and in Baptiſme. which is no more to ſay, but that it is impoſſible to be baptized againe, and thereby to be renouated and illuminated, to die, be buried, and riſe againe the ſecond time in Chriſt, in ſo eaſie and perfect penance and cleanſing of ſinnes, as that firſt ſacrament of generation did yeld: which applieth Chriſtes death in ſuch ample maner to the receiuers, that it taketh avvay al paines due for ſinnes before committed: and therfore requireth no further penance afterward, for the ſinnes before committed, al being vvaſhed away by the force of that Sacrament duely taken. S. Auguſtine calleth the remiſsion in Baptiſme, Magnam indulgentiam, a great pardon. Enchirid. c. 64. [7] The Apoſtle therfore warneth them, that if they fall from their faith, and from Chriſtes grace and lavv which they once receiued in their Baptiſme, they may not looke to haue any more that firſt great and large remedie applied vnto them, nor no man els that ſinneth after Baptiſme: though the other penance, which is called the Second table after ſinners ſhipwracke, [8]which is a more paineful medicine for ſinne then Baptiſme, requiring much faſting, praying, and other afflictions corporal, is open not onely to other ſinners, but to al once baptized, Heretikes, or oppugners of the truth malitiouſly and of purpoſe or what way ſo euer, during this life. See S. Cyprian ep. 52. S. Ambroſe vpon this place. S. Auguſtine cont. ep. Parm. li. 2. c. 13. and ep. 50. S. Damaſcene li. 4. c. 10.

notes.text: The Nouatians (as al Heretikes) made Scripture the ground of their heresie.

annotations.title: God is not vniuſt.
annotations.text: ◦ It is a world to ſee, vvhat wringing & writhing the Proteſtants make, to ſhift them ſelues from the euidence of theſe wordes, which make it moſt cleere to all not blinded in pride and contention, that good workes be meritorious, and the very cauſe of ſaluation, ſo far, that God ſhould be vniuſt, if he rendered not heauen for the ſame. Reuera grandis iniuſtitia Dei (ſaith S. Hierom) Si tantum peccata puniret, & bona opera non ſuſciperet. That is, In deede great vvere Gods iniuſtice, if he vvould onely puniſh ſinnes, and vvould not receiue good workes. Li. 2. cont. Iouin. c. 2.

notes.text: Gods iustice in rewarding meritorious workes.
